readings.c1s1:
''wen'', < AS. *''bismerwian'', ''besmyrian'' (= MHG. ''besmirwen''), besmear, < ''be-'' + ''smyrwan'', ''smierwan'', smear: see ''be-''<sup>1</sup> and ''smear''.] To smear over or about; bedaub; overspread with any viscous matter, or with any soft substance that adheres; hence, to foul; soil; sully.
{{smaller block|<poem>My honour would not let ingratitude
So much ''besmear'' it.
</poem>{{right|''Shak.'', M. of V., v. i.}}
<poem>His dear friends Acates and Acanthes
Lie in the field ''besmired'' in their bloods.
</poem>{{right|''Chapman'', Blind Beggar.}}
Her gushing blood the pavement all ''besmear’d.''
{{right|''Dryden.''}}}}

'''besmearer''' (bē-smēr′ėr), ''n.'' One who besmears.

'''besmirch''' (bē-smėrch′), ''v. t.'' [< ''be-''<sup>1</sup> + ''smirch''.] To soil; discolor, as with soot or mud; hence, to sully; obscure. [The figurative use is now the more common one.]
{{smaller block|<poem>Our gayness, and our gilt, are all ''besmirch’d''
With rainy marching in the painful field.
</poem>{{right|''Shak.'', Hen. V., iv. 3.}}
The dishonor that ''besmirches'' the husband of a faithless woman.
{{right|''Hawthorne'', Scarlet Letter, p. 87.}}}}

'''besmoke''' (bē-smōk′), ''v. t.'' [< ME. ''besmoken'', < ''be-''<sup>1</sup> + ''smoken'', smoke: see ''be-''<sup>1</sup> and ''smoke''.]
readings.c1s2:
'''1.''' To befoul or fill with smoke.—'''2.''' To harden or dry in smoke. ''Johnson.''—'''3.''' To fumigate. [Rare.]

'''besmooth''' (bē̤-smöᴛ̵ʜ′), ''v. t.'' [< ''be-''<sup>1</sup> + ''smooth.''] To make smooth. ''Chapman.''

'''besmotered†''', ''pp.'' [ME., pp. of *''besmoteren''; appar. freq. of ''besmut'', which, however, does not appear in ME.] Smutted; spotted; made dirty.
{{smaller block|<poem>A gepoun
Al ''bysmotered'' with his habergeoun.</poem>
{{right|''Chaucer'', Gen. Prol. to C. T., l. 76.}}}}

'''besmut''' (bē̤-smut′), ''v. t.''; pret. and pp. ''besmutted'', ppr. ''besmutting.'' [< ''be-''<sup>1</sup> + ''smut.''] To blacken with smut; foul with soot.

'''besmutch''' (bē̤-smuch′), ''v. t.'' [< ''be-''<sup>1</sup> + ''smutch.''] To besmirch. ''Carlyle.''

'''besnow''' (bē̤-snō′), ''v. t.'' [With altered vowel (after ''snow''), for earlier ''besnew'', < ME. ''besnewen'', < AS. ''besnīwan'' (= MHG. ''besnīen'', G. ''beschneien''), < ''be-'' + ''snīwan'', snow: see ''be-''<sup>1</sup> and ''snow.''] To cover with or as with snow; whiten.
{{smaller block|A third thy white and small hand shall ''besnow.''
{{right|''Carew'', To Lady Anne Hay.}}}}

'''besnuff''' (bē̤-snuf′), ''v. t.'' [< ''be-''<sup>1</sup> + ''snuff.''] To befoul with snuff. [Rare.]
{{smaller block|Unwashed her hands, and much ''besnuffed'' her face.
{{right|''Young'', Satires, vi.}}}}

'''besognio†''', ''n.'' See ''bisognio.''

'''besoil''' (bē̤-soil′), ''v. t.'' [< ME. ''besoylen'', < ''be-''<sup>1</sup> + ''soilen'', soil: see ''be-''<sup>1</sup> and ''soil.''] To soil; stain; sully.
{{smaller block|Venerable too is the rugged face, all weather-tanned, ''besoiled'', with its rude intelligence.
{{right|''Carlyle'', Sartor Resartus, iii. 4.}}}}
readings.c1s3:
¶
'''besom''' (bē′zum), ''n.'' [< ME. ''besum, besem, besme,'' a broom, a rod, < AS. ''besema, besma,'' a rod, in pl. a bundle of twigs or rods used as a broom, also as an instrument of punishment, = OFries. ''besma'' = OD. ''bessem,'' D. ''bezem'' = LG. ''bessen'' = OHG. ''besamo,'' MHG. ''beseme,'' G. ''besen,'' a broom, a rod; orig. perhaps a twig, hence a bundle of twigs, a broom.] '''1.''' A brush of twigs for sweeping; hence, a broom of any kind.
{{smaller block|I will sweep it with the ''besom'' of destruction, saith the Lord of hosts. {{right|Is. xiv. 23.}}
The Lord Bacon was wont to commend the advice of the plain old man at Buxton, that sold ''besoms.''
{{right|''Bacon’s Apophthegms,'' p. 190.}}
There is little to the rake to get after the ''bissome.''
{{right|''Scotch proverb,'' in Ray (1678), p. 390.}}}}
'''2.''' A name given to the common broom of Europe, ''Cytisus scoparius,'' and to the heather, ''Calluna vulgaris,'' because both are used for besoms. —'''3.''' [Pron. biz′um.] A contemptuous epithet for a low, worthless woman. [Scotch.]

'''besom''' (bē′zum), ''v. t.'' [< ''besom, n.''] To sweep as with a besom. ''Cowper.'' [Rare.]

'''besomer''' (bē′zum-ėr), ''n.'' One who uses a besom.

'''besoothment''' (bẹ̄-söᴛ̵ʜ′ment), ''n.'' [< *''besoothe'' (not in use) (< ''be-''<sup>1</sup> + ''soothe'') + ''-ment.''] That which yields consolation; solace; comfort. ''Quarterly Rev.'' [Rare.]

'''besort†''' (bẹ̄-sôrt′), ''v. t.'' [< ''be-''<sup>1</sup> + ''sort.''] To suit; fit; become.
{{smaller block|Such men as may ''besort'' your age. {{right|''Shak.,'' Lear, i. 4.}}}}

'''besort†''' (bẹ̄-sôrt′), ''n.'' [< ''besort, v.''] Something fitting or appropriate; suitable company.
readings.c1s4:
{{smaller block|<poem>I crave fit disposition for my wife, . . .
With such accommodation and ''besort''
As levels with her breeding.</poem>{{right|''Shak.'', Othello, i. 3.}}}}

'''besot''' (bē-sot′), ''v. t.''; pret. and pp. ''besotted'', ppr. ''besotting''. [< ''be-''<sup>1</sup> + ''sot''.] '''1.''' To infatuate; make a dotard of.
readings.c2s2:
¶
'''besour''' (bē-sour′), ''v. t.'' [< ''be-''<sup>1</sup> + ''sour.''] To make sour. ''Hammond.''

'''besouth''' (bē-south′), ''prep.'' [< ME. ''be-sowth''; < ''be-''<sup>2</sup> + ''south.'' Cf. ''benorth.''] To the south of. [Scotch.]

'''bespangle''' (bē-spang′gl), ''v. t.'' [< ''be-''<sup>1</sup> + ''spangle.''] To adorn with spangles; dot or sprinkle with small glittering objects.
{{smaller block|<poem>Not Berenice’s lock first rose so bright,
The heav’ns ''bespangling'' with dishevell’d light.</poem>
{{right|''Pope'', R. of the L., v. 130.}}}}

'''bespat''' (bē-spat′). Preterit of ''bespit.''

'''bespatter''' (bē-spat′ėr), ''v. t.'' [< ''be-''<sup>1</sup> + ''spatter.''] '''1.''' To soil by spattering; sprinkle with anything liquid, or with any wet or adhesive substance.—'''2.''' Figuratively, to asperse with calumny or reproach.
{{smaller block|Whom never faction could ''bespatter.'' ''Swift'', On Poetry.}}

'''bespattle†''' (bē-spat′l), ''v. t.'' [< ''be-''<sup>1</sup> + ''spattle.''] To spit on. ''Bp. Bale.''

'''bespawl†''' (bē-spâl′), ''v. t.'' [< ''be-''<sup>1</sup> + ''spawl.''] To soil or make foul with or as with spittle.
{{smaller block|<poem>''Bespawls''
The conscious time with humorous foam and brawls.</poem>
{{right|''B. Jonson'', Poetaster, v. 1.}}

This remonstrant would invest himself conditionally with all the rheum of the town, that he might have sufficient to ''bespawl'' his brethren.
{{right|''Milton'', Def. of Humb. Remonst.}}}}
readings.c3s2:
{{smaller block|<poem>His cup-bearer, . . . mightst ''bespice'' a cup,
To give mine enemy a lasting wink.</poem>
{{right|''Shak.'', W. T., i. 2.}}}}

¶
'''bespirt†''', ''v. t.'' See ''bespurt.''

'''bespit''' (bẹ̄-spit′), ''v. t.''; pret. ''bespit'', ''bespat'', pp. ''bespit'', ''bespitten'', ''bespitted'', ppr. ''bespitting.'' [< ME. ''bispitten'', < ''bi-'' + ''spitten'', spit: see ''be-''<sup>1</sup> and ''spit'', and cf. ''bespet.''] To spit upon; soil with spittle.

'''bespoke''' (bẹ̄-spōk′). Preterit and past participle of ''bespeak.''

'''bespot''' (bẹ̄-spot′), ''v. t.'' [< ME. ''bispotten'', < ''bi-'' + ''spotten'', spot: see ''be-''<sup>1</sup> and ''spot.''] To make spots on; mark with spots; cover with or as with blots or blemishes.

{{smaller block|''Bespotted'' so with sin. {{right|''Drayton'', Matilda to K. John.}}}}

'''bespread''' (bẹ̄-spred′), ''v. t.'' [< ''be-''<sup>1</sup> + ''spread.''] To spread over; cover with.

{{smaller block|<poem>His nuptial bed,
With curious needles wrought, and painted flowers ''bespread.''</poem>
{{right|''Dryden.''}}}}

'''bespreng''' (bẹ̄-spreng′), ''v. t.'' [< ME. ''besprengen'', ''bisprengen'' (pp. ''besprenged'', ''bespreynt'', etc.), < AS. ''besprengan'' (= D. and G. ''besprengen''), besprinkle, < ''be-'' + ''sprengan'', sprinkle: see ''be-''<sup>1</sup> and ''spreng'', and cf. ''besprinkle.''] '''1.''' To sprinkle over; besprinkle: as, “''besprent'' with teares,” ''Mir. for Mags.'', p. 26.

{{smaller block|The floor with tassels of fir was ''besprent.''
{{right|''Longfellow'', Wayside Inn, King Olaf, iv.}}}}

'''2.''' To spread; scatter.

{{smaller block|His silver tresses thin ''besprent.''
{{right|''T. Warton'', Grave of King Arthur.}}}}

{{smaller block|I will sweep it with the ''besom'' of destruction, saith the Lord of hosts. {{right|Is. xiv. 23.}}}}
{{smaller block|The Lord Bacon was wont to commend the advice of the plain old man at Buxton, that sold ''besoms.''

'''besomer''' (bē′zum-ėr), ''n.'' One who uses a besom.

'''besort†''' (bẹ̄-sôrt′), ''n.''   [< ''besort, v.'']   Something fitting or appropriate; suitable company.
<poem>I crave fit disposition for my wife, . . .
With such accommodation and ''besort''
As levels with her breeding.</poem>{{right|''Shak.'', Othello, i. 3.}}

'''besot''' (bē-sot′), ''v. t.''; pret. and pp. ''besotted'', ppr. ''besotting''.   [< ''be-''<sup>1</sup> + ''sot''.]   '''1.''' To infatuate; make a dotard of. {{smaller block|A fellow sincerely ''besotted'' on his own wife.
{{right|''B. Jonson'', Every Man out of his Humour, Pref.}}}}
'''2.''' To stupefy; affect with mental or moral stupidity or blindness.
{{smaller block|A weak and ''besotted'' prince—who had . . . produced a revolt in which six thousand lives were lost—is permitted, unmolested and in safety, to leave the city.
{{right|''Everett'', Orations, I. 517.}}}}
'''3.''' To make sottish, as with drink; make a sot of.
{{smaller block|Permitted . . . to ''besot'' themselves in the company of their favourite revellers. {{right|''Macaulay'', Hist. Eng., ii.}}}}

'''besotment''' (bẹ̄-sot′mẹnt), ''n.''   [< ''besot'' + ''-ment.'']   The act of making one’s self sottish by drink; the state of being besotted.
{{smaller block|The debasing habit of unsocial ''besotment'' is not brought under the eyes of his superior. {{right|''Bulwer.''}}}}

'''besotted''' (bẹ̄-sot′ed), ''p. a.'' '''1.''' Characterized by or indicative of stupidity; stupid; infatuated.
{{smaller block|''Besotted'', base ingratitude. {{right|''Milton'', Comus, l. 778.}}}}
{{smaller block|Historical painting had sunk . . . on the north into the patient devotion of ''besotted'' lives to delineations of bricks and fogs, fat cattle and ditch water. {{right|''Ruskin.''}}}}
'''2.''' Made sottish by drink; stupefied by habitual intoxication.

'''besottedly''' (bẹ̄-sot′ed-li), ''adv.'' In a besotted or foolish manner.

'''besottedness''' (bẹ̄-sot′ed-nes), ''n.'' The state of being besotted; stupidity; arrant folly; infatuation.

'''besottingly''' (bẹ̄-sot′ing-li), ''adv.'' In a besotting manner.

'''besought''' (bẹ̄-sôt′). Preterit and past participle of ''beseech.''

'''besour''' (bē-sour′), ''v. t.''   [< ''be-''<sup>1</sup> + ''sour.'']   To make sour.   ''Hammond.''

'''besouth''' (bē-south′), ''prep.''   [< ME. ''be-sowth''; < ''be-''<sup>2</sup> + ''south.'' Cf. ''benorth.'']   To the south of. [Scotch.]

'''bespangle''' (bē-spang′gl), ''v. t.''   [< ''be-''<sup>1</sup> + ''spangle.'']   To adorn with spangles; dot or sprinkle with small glittering objects.
{{smaller block|<poem>Not Berenice’s lock first rose so bright,
The heav’ns ''bespangling'' with dishevell’d light.</poem>
{{right|''Pope'', R. of the L., v. 130.}}}}

'''bespat''' (bē-spat′). Preterit of ''bespit.''

'''bespatter''' (bē-spat′ėr), ''v. t.''   [< ''be-''<sup>1</sup> + ''spatter.'']   '''1.''' To soil by spattering; sprinkle with anything liquid, or with any wet or adhesive substance.—'''2.''' Figuratively, to asperse with calumny or reproach.
{{smaller block|Whom never faction could ''bespatter.''
{{right|''Swift'', On Poetry.}}}}

'''bespattle†''' (bē-spat′l), ''v. t.''   [< ''be-''<sup>1</sup> + ''spattle.'']   To spit on.   ''Bp. Bale.''

'''bespawl†''' (bē-spâl′), ''v. t.''   [< ''be-''<sup>1</sup> + ''spawl.'']   To soil or make foul with or as with spittle.
{{smaller block|<poem>''Bespawls''
The conscious time with humorous foam and brawls.</poem>
{{right|''B. Jonson'', Poetaster, v. 1.}}}}
{{smaller block|This remonstrant would invest himself conditionally with all the rheum of the town, that he might have sufficient to ''bespawl'' his brethren.
{{right|''Milton'', Def. of Humb. Remonst.}}}}

'''bespeak''' (bē-spēk′), ''v.''; pret. ''bespoke'' (formerly ''bespake''), pp. ''bespoken'', ''bespoke'', ppr. ''bespeaking''.   [< ME. ''bespeken'', ''bispeken'', speak, agree upon, complain, < AS. ''besprecan'', complain (= OS. ''bisprekan'' = OFries. ''bispreka'' = D. ''bespreken'' = OHG. ''bisprehhan'', MHG. G. ''besprechen'', bespeak), < ''be-'' + ''sprecan'', speak: see ''be-''<sup>1</sup> and ''speak''.]   '''I.''' ''trans.'' '''1.''' To speak for beforehand; engage in advance; make arrangements for: as, to ''bespeak'' a place in a theater.
{{smaller block|Staying in Paul’s Churchyard, to ''bespeak'' Ogilby’s Æsop’s Fables and Tully’s Officys to be bound for me.
{{right|''Pepys'', Diary, I. 138.}}}}
{{smaller block|’Tis very true, ma’am; every thing is fixed, and the wedding liveries ''bespoke''.
{{right|''Sheridan'', School for Scandal, i. 1.}}}}
'''2.''' To stipulate, solicit, or ask for, as a favor: as, to ''bespeak'' a calm hearing.
{{smaller block|This is a sinister and politic kind of charity, whereby we seem to ''bespeak'' the pities of men in the like occasions.
{{right|''Sir T. Browne'', Religio Medici, ii. 2.}}}}
'''3†.''' To forebode; foretell.
{{smaller block|They started fears, ''bespoke'' dangers, and formed ominous prognosticks, to scare the allies.
{{right|''Swift.''}}}}
'''4.''' To speak to; address. [In this sense mostly poetical.]
{{smaller block|He thus the queen ''bespoke''.
{{right|''Dryden.''}}}}
'''5.''' To betoken; show; indicate, as by signs.
{{smaller block|When the abbot of St. Martin was born, he had so little the figure of a man that it ''bespoke'' him rather a monster.
{{right|''Locke.''}}}}
{{smaller block|<poem>His face ''bespeaks''
A deep and simple meekness.</poem>
{{right|''Wordsworth'', The Borderers, i.}}}}

{{smaller block|The object, alike paltry and impossible, of this ambition, ''bespoke'' the narrow mind.
{{right|''Motley'', Dutch Republic, II. 513.}}}}

'''II.†''' ''intrans.'' To speak up or out; exclaim; speak.
{{smaller block|Until their Lord himself ''bespake'', and bid them go.
{{right|''Milton'', Nativity, vi.}}}}
{{smaller block|And thus the chief ''bespake''. {{right|''Cowper'', Iliad, ii. 201.}}}}

'''bespeak''' (bē-spēk′), ''n.''   [< ''bespeak'', ''v.'', 1.]   Among actors in Great Britain, a benefit: so called from the bespeaking of patronage by the actors, or of the play by the patrons. See ''benefit'', 5.

'''bespeaker''' (bē-spē′kėr), ''n.'' One who bespeaks.

'''bespeaking''' (bē-spē′king), ''n.''   [Verbal n. of ''bespeak''.]   The act of speaking for or soliciting; solicitation.
{{smaller block|A preface, therefore, which is but a ''bespeaking'' of favour, is altogether useless. {{right|''Dryden'', Hind and Panther, Pref.}}}}

'''bespeckle''' (bē-spek′l), ''v. t.''   [< ''be-''<sup>1</sup> + ''speckle''.]   To mark with speckles, spots, or bright patches.
{{smaller block|''Bespeckled'' her with . . . gaudy allurements.
{{right|''Milton'', Reformation in Eng., i.}}}}

'''bespend†''' (bẹ̄-spend′), ''v. t.''   [< ''be-''<sup>1</sup> + ''spend''.]   To expend; bestow; employ.
{{smaller block|<poem>All his craft
''Bespent'' about the bed.</poem>
{{right|''Chapman'', Odyssey, viii.}}}}

'''bespet†''', ''v. t.''   [ME. ''bespeten'' (weak verb, pp. ''bespet'', ''bespat''), < ''be-''<sup>1</sup> + ''speten'', < AS. ''spǣtan'', spit: see ''spit'', and cf. ''bespit''.]   To bespit.

'''bespew''' (bē-spū′), ''v. t.''   [< ''be-''<sup>1</sup> + ''spew''.]   To spew or vomit on.

'''bespice''' (bē-spīs′), ''v. t.''   [< ''be-''<sup>1</sup> + ''spice''.]   To season with spices or drugs; hence, to drug; poison.
{{smaller block|<poem>Ay, and thou,</poem>}}
<poem>His cup-bearer, . . . mightst ''bespice'' a cup,
To give mine enemy a lasting wink.</poem>
{{smaller block|{{right|''Shak.'', W. T., i. 2.}}}}

'''bespirt†''', ''v. t.'' See ''bespurt.''

'''bespit''' (bẹ̄-spit′), ''v. t.''; pret. ''bespit'', ''bespat'', pp. ''bespit'', ''bespitten'', ''bespitted'', ppr. ''bespitting.''   [< ME. ''bispitten'', < ''bi-'' + ''spitten'', spit: see ''be-''<sup>1</sup> and ''spit'', and cf. ''bespet.'']   To spit upon; soil with spittle.

'''bespoke''' (bẹ̄-spōk′). Preterit and past participle of ''bespeak.''

'''bespot''' (bẹ̄-spot′), ''v. t.''   [< ME. ''bispotten'', < ''bi-'' + ''spotten'', spot: see ''be-''<sup>1</sup> and ''spot.'']   To make spots on; mark with spots; cover with or as with blots or blemishes.

{{smaller block|''Bespotted'' so with sin. {{right|''Drayton'', Matilda to K. John.}}}}

'''bespread''' (bẹ̄-spred′), ''v. t.''   [< ''be-''<sup>1</sup> + ''spread.'']   To spread over; cover with.

<poem>His nuptial bed,
With curious needles wrought, and painted flowers ''bespread.''</poem>
{{smaller block|{{right|''Dryden.''}}}}

'''bespreng''' (bẹ̄-spreng′), ''v. t.''   [< ME. ''besprengen'', ''bisprengen'' (pp. ''besprenged'', ''bespreynt'', etc.), < AS. ''besprengan'' (= D. and G. ''besprengen''), besprinkle, < ''be-'' + ''sprengan'', sprinkle: see ''be-''<sup>1</sup> and ''spreng'', and cf. ''besprinkle.'']   '''1.''' To sprinkle over; besprinkle: as, “''besprent'' with teares,” ''Mir. for Mags.'', p. 26.

{{smaller block|The floor with tassels of fir was ''besprent.''
{{right|''Longfellow'', Wayside Inn, King Olaf, iv.}}}}

'''2.''' To spread; scatter.

{{smaller block|His silver tresses thin ''besprent.''
{{right|''T. Warton'', Grave of King Arthur.}}}} [Obsolete except in the perfect participle ''besprent.'']

'''besprent''' (bẹ̄-sprent′), ''p. a.''   [Pp. of ''bespreng.'']   Besprinkled.
{{smaller block|In the flower-''besprent'' meadows his genius we trace.
{{right|''Wordsworth'', At Vallombrosa.}}}}

'''besprinkle''' (bẹ̄-spring′kl), ''v. t.''   [< ''be-''<sup>1</sup> + ''sprinkle.'' Cf. ''bespreng.'']   To sprinkle over; scatter over: as, to ''besprinkle'' with dust.
{{smaller block|Herodotus . . . hath ''besprinkled'' his work with many fabulosities.
{{right|''Sir T. Browne.''}}}}
{{smaller block|''Besprinkles'' with Cimmerian dew.
{{right|''Pope'', Dunciad, iii. 4.}}}}

'''besprinkler''' (bẹ̄-spring′klėr), ''n.'' One who besprinkles.

'''bespurt, bespirt†''' (bẹ̄-spėrt′), ''v. t.''   [< ''be-''<sup>1</sup> + ''spurt.'']   To spurt out or over; throw out in a stream or streams.
{{smaller block|Well ''bespurted'' with his own holy water.
{{right|''Milton'', Def. of Humb. Remonst.}}}}

'''bespurtle†''' (bẹ̄-spėr′tl), ''v. t.''   [< ''be-''<sup>1</sup> + ''spurtle.'']   To bespatter, as with contumely; asperse.
{{smaller block|I give thy dogged sullennes free libertie: trot about, and ''bespurtle'' whom thou pleasest.
{{right|''Marston and Webster'', The Malcontent, i. 2.}}}}

'''besputter''' (bẹ̄-sput′ėr), ''v. t.''   [< ''be-''<sup>1</sup> + ''sputter.'']   To sputter over.

'''Besselian''' (be-sel′yan), ''a.'' Pertaining to or originated by the German astronomer Friedrich Wilhelm Bessel (1784–1846).—'''Besselian function.''' {{smaller|Same as ''Bessel’s function'' (which see, under ''function'').}}
